verses.zh: 「你要注意亚笔月，向耶和华―你的　神守逾越节，因为耶和华―你的　神在亚笔月夜间领你出埃及。
verses.en: Observe the month Abib[NOTE:1] and keep the Passover to the Lord your God, for in that month[NOTE:2] he[NOTE:3] brought you out of Egypt by night.
notes: The month Abib, later called Nisan (Neh 2:1; Esth 3:7), corresponds to March-April in the modern calendar.
Heb “in the month Abib.” The demonstrative “that” has been used in the translation for stylistic reasons.
Heb “the Lord your God.” The pronoun has been used in the translation for stylistic reasons to avoid redundancy.
verses.commentary:
16:1-12 These verses discuss the three annual feast days that are to be observed at the central sanctuary. This
same information is found in

- Exod. 23:14-19

- Exod. 34:18-26

- Lev. 23:1-44 (includes several other special days)

- Numbers 28-29 (includes several other special days)

These annual feast days were Israel's way to remember yearly YHWH's great acts, and provided a way to
teach the next generation.

SPECIAL TOPIC: FEASTS OF ISRAEL

16:1 "Observe" This is such a recurrent term (BDB 1036, KB 1581, Qal INFINITIVE ABSOLUTE)
in Deuteronomy- 73 times! This chapter is written in the same Hebraic style as the Ten Commandments of chapter 5.

▣ "month" This is the same root as "new moon" (BDB 294 I).

SPECIAL TOPIC: ANE CALENDARS

▣ "Abib" This word means "new grain" (BDB 1), which would denote the first ripened sheaves of
barley. It was the Canaanite designation for the time period of March‒April. In the Babylonian calendar the word
Nisan is used for this time period. It was considered the first month in the Hebrew calendar (cf. Ecxod. 13:4; 33:15).

Surprisingly, this month is related to the feast of

- Unleavened Bread, which was an additional feast linked to the Passover, cf. Exod. 12:5,15-20; 13:1-10; Lev. 23:6-8
(i.e. seven days long after Passover)

- Passover in Lev. 23:4-5; Deut. 16:1-8 (i.e. one day)

These two feasts were later joined into one eight day feast.

SPECIAL TOPIC: PASSOVER

▣ "celebrate" This common VERB, "do," "make" (BDB 793, KB 1581) is used several
times in chapter 16 and is translated several ways:

- "celebrate," Deut. 16:1,10,13

- "shall be," Deut. 16:8

- "shall be careful to observe," Deut. 16:12

- "shall not. . .make," Deut. 16:21

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE PASSOVER

▣ "by night" When the Death Angel passed over at night (BDB 538), Pharaoh said, "go now"
(cf. Exod.12:31-33). The Israelites left immediately.

SPECIAL TOPIC: DEATH ANGEL

verses.zh: 你当在耶和华所选择要立为他名的居所，从牛群羊群中，将逾越节的祭牲献给耶和华―你的　神。
verses.en: You must sacrifice the Passover animal[NOTE:1] (from the flock or the herd) to the Lord your God in the place where he[NOTE:2] chooses to locate his name.
notes: Heb “sacrifice the Passover” (so NASB). The word “animal” has been supplied in the translation for clarity.
Heb “the Lord.” See note on “he” in the previous verse.
verses.commentary:
16:2 "from the flock and the herd" Originally it was only a sheep or a goat (cf. Exod. 12:5). In the special Passovers
of Hezekiah and Josiah, they offered more types of animals, possibly peace offerings, 2 Chr. 30:24; 35:7.

What does "and the herd" mean? Only sheep or goats were part of the Passover ritual. The Hebrew
CONJUNCTION (BDB 251-255) can mean "and" or "or." But this does not answer the question, "Why is
an animal from the herd an option?" The Tyndale OT Commentary by J. A. Thompson, p. 194, suggests that the
herd sacrifices were connected with the seven day Feast of Unleavened Bread from ancient times and this is why
Hezekiah and Josiah had herd animals offered (i.e. peace offerings) as a way to provide food for the celebrants.

It is just possible that "the herd" refers to

- offering of the firstborn, which is mentioned in the same context (cf. Exod. 22:29; 34:20)

- the freewill offering of v. 16 ‒ attendees of the three annual feasts should not come "empty-handed" (cf. v. 17)

SPECIAL TOPIC: PEACE OFFERING

▣ "in the place where the Lord chooses to establish His name" In Egypt this
was a family service; in Deuteronomy it has been reserved for central sanctuary worship (cf. Deut. 12:5,11,13,14,18,21,26;
14:23,25; 15:20; 16:2,6,7,11,15,16; 17:8,10; 18:6; 23:16; 26:2; 31:11).

verses.zh: 你吃这祭牲，不可吃有酵的饼；七日之内要吃无酵饼，就是困苦饼―你本是急忙出了埃及地―要叫你一生一世记念你从埃及地出来的日子。
verses.en: You must not eat any yeast with it; for seven days you must eat bread made without yeast, as symbolic of affliction,[NOTE:1] for you came out of Egypt hurriedly. You must do this so you will remember for the rest of your lives the day you came out of the land of Egypt.
notes: Heb “bread of affliction.” Their affliction was part of the cause of why they ate this kind of bread. It could be understood as “the sort of bread made under oppressive circumstances.” The kind of bread was used to symbolize and remind of their affliction.
verses.commentary:
16:3 "unleavened bread" The Israelites could not wait to depart until morning for the bread to rise. This detail of the exodus
night gave rise to the Exodus' Passover feast being combined with an agricultural feast (cf. Exod. 12:15-20; 23:14-17; 34:18).

Leaven, which was regularly used in sacrificial items (cf. Lev. 7:13; 23:17), became a symbol of sin and
rebellion. The fermentation was viewed in this symbolic feast as Israel's opportunity on an individual basis to examine their
lives for any hint of rebellion or disobedience to YHWH. As the Day of Atonement (Leviticus 16) functioned on a national
level, the Feast of Unleavened Bread functioned on an individual or family level.

This annual required feast being combined with the Passover feast kept the gracious deliverance of
YHWH ever before the minds and hearts of His people. As grace and promise provided deliverance from Egypt, so Israel
depended on these unchanging divine characteristics to save her as the years went by (cf. Deut. 4:9).

SPECIAL TOPIC: LEAVEN

▣ "bread of affliction" See Exod. 12:8.

▣ "(for you came out of the land of Egypt in haste)" The Israelites left Egypt in haste at Pharaoh's request
(cf. Exod.12:31-33).

▣ "that you remember. . .Egypt" The Passover has historical and theological significance. In Egypt
the Passover experience was family oriented; in Deuteronomy it foreshadowed the coming central sanctuary service; in
Jesus' day it became a combination of both (part at the temple and part at home or where pilgrims were staying while
in Jerusalem).

SPECIAL TOPIC: PASSOVER

verses.zh: 在你四境之内，七日不可见面酵，头一日晚上所献的肉，一点不可留到早晨。
verses.en: There must not be a scrap of yeast within your land[NOTE:1] for seven days, nor can any of the meat you sacrifice on the evening of the first day remain until the next morning.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “leaven must not be seen among you in all your border.”
Heb “remain all night until the morning” (so KJV, ASV). This has been simplified in the translation for stylistic reasons.
verses.commentary:
16:4 Remember, Moses is addressing, for the most part, the children of the exodus generation. This verse implies
that every generation should put themselves in the place of that first generation who experienced the power and presence
of YHWH, yet rebelled and died in the wilderness. Each of the annual feasts were to help Israel trust more in YHWH's presence
and provision. He was with them and for them, as He had been with their ancestors.

verses.zh: 在耶和华―你　神所赐的各城中，你不可献逾越节的祭；
verses.en: You may not sacrifice the Passover in just any of your villages[NOTE:1] that the Lord your God is giving you,
notes: Heb “gates.”
verses.commentary:
16:5 "in any of your towns" This is literally "gates" (BDB 1044, cf. Deut. 12:15,17,21), thereby referring to a future
time after Israel had conquered Canaan (cf. Deut. 16:18).

verses.zh: 只当在耶和华―你　神所选择要立为他名的居所，晚上日落的时候，乃是你出埃及的时候，献逾越节的祭。
verses.en: but you must sacrifice it[NOTE:1] in the evening in[NOTE:2] the place where he[NOTE:3] chooses to locate his name, at sunset, the time of day you came out of Egypt.
notes: Heb “the Passover.” The translation uses a pronoun to avoid redundancy in English.
The MT reading אֶל (ʾel, “unto”) before “the place” should, following Smr, Syriac, Targums, and Vulgate, be omitted in favor of ב (bet; בַּמָּקוֹם, bammaqom), “in the place.”
Heb “the Lord your God.” See note on “he” in 16:1.
verses.commentary: 16:6 "in the evening at sunset" For the Israelites this was the beginning of a new day (cf. Genesis 1, cf. Exod. 12:6. ).

verses.zh: 当在耶和华―你　神所选择的地方把肉烤了吃（烤：或译煮），次日早晨就回到你的帐棚去。
verses.en: You must cook[NOTE:1] and eat it in the place the Lord your God chooses; you may return the next morning to your tents.
notes: The rules that governed the Passover meal are found in Exod 12:1-51, and Deut 16:1-8. The word translated “cook” (בָּשַׁל, bashal) here is translated “boil” in other places (e.g. Exod 23:19, 1 Sam 2:13-15). This would seem to contradict Exod 12:9 where the Israelites are told not to eat the Passover sacrifice raw or boiled. However, 2 Chr 35:13 recounts the celebration of a Passover feast during the reign of Josiah, and explains that the people “cooked (בָּשַׁל, bashal) the Passover sacrifices over the open fire.” The use of בָּשַׁל (bashal) with “fire” (אֵשׁ, ʾesh) suggests that the word could be used to speak of boiling or roasting.
verses.commentary:
16:7 "You shall cook and eat it" The Hebrew can mean "boil" or "cook" (BDB 143, KB 164, Piel
PERFECT with waw), but because of Exod. 12:8-9, it must be a general term for "cook."

Most of the sacrifices were "boiled" (cf. Exod. 29:31; Lev. 8:31; Num. 6:15; 1 Sam. 2:13). The Passover sacrifice was to be
roasted with fire (Exod. 12:8-9; 2 Chr. 35:13). It is possible, like 2 Chr. 35:13, that both ways of cooking were used.

- boiled ‒ the herd of v. 2

- roasted ‒ the flock of v. 2

See F. F. Bruce, Answers to Questions, pp. 213-214. This is one of my favorite books on Bible difficulties.
F. F. Bruce handles the texts so well. I highly recommend this book to you!

▣ "you are to return to your tents" This can mean:

- the wilderness wandering setting (or at least on the plains of Moab)

- the pilgrims going to Jerusalem stayed in tents during these seven feast days

- it is an idiom meaning "return to your homes

verses.zh: 你要吃无酵饼六日，第七日要向耶和华―你的　神守严肃会，不可做工。」
verses.en: You must eat bread made without yeast for six days. The seventh day you are to hold an assembly for the Lord your God; you must not do any work on that day.[NOTE:1]
notes: The words “on that day” are not in the Hebrew text; they are supplied in the translation for clarification (cf. TEV, NLT).
verses.commentary:
16:8 "a solemn assembly to the Lord your God" The festival ended with a corporate worship setting
(cf. Exod. 12:16, "a holy assembly"). One purpose for the central sanctuary was to develop a sense of corporate identity and
community.

verses.zh: 「你要计算七七日：从你开镰收割禾稼时算起，共计七七日。
verses.en: You must count seven weeks; you must begin to count them[NOTE:1] from the time you begin to harvest the standing grain.
notes: Heb “the seven weeks.” The translation uses a pronoun to avoid redundancy in English.

verses.zh: 你要照耶和华―你　神所赐你的福，手里拿着甘心祭，献在耶和华―你的　神面前，守七七节。
verses.en: Then you are to celebrate the Feast of Weeks[NOTE:1] before the Lord your God with the voluntary offering[NOTE:2] that you will bring, in proportion to how he[NOTE:3] has blessed you.
notes: The Hebrew phrase חַג שָׁבֻעוֹת (khag shavuʿot) is otherwise known in the OT (Exod 23:16) as קָצִיר (qatsir, “harvest”) and in the NT as πεντηχοστή (pentēhchostē, “Pentecost”).
Heb “the sufficiency of the offering of your hand.”
Heb “the Lord your God.” See note on “he” in 16:1.
verses.commentary:
16:10 "the Feast of Weeks" This is also called

- the Feast of Harvest in Exod. 23:16

- the Feast of First Fruits in Num. 28:26

- Later, it became Pentecost (rabbinically linked to the giving of the Law on Mt. Sinai), which means "fifty days."

It was the May ‒ June harvest festival or the time of the wheat harvest. YHWH, not Ba'al, was the provider!

SPECIAL TOPIC: FEASTS OF ISRAEL, I. D. 2.

▣ "a freewill offering" This allowed the people to bring an offering in accordance to how much the
Lord had blessed each one (cf. Deut. 16:17). This is a universal principle of giving (cf. 2 Corinthians 8-9).

verses.zh: 你和你儿女、仆婢，并住在你城里的利未人，以及在你们中间寄居的与孤儿寡妇，都要在耶和华―你　神所选择立为他名的居所，在耶和华―你的　神面前欢乐。
verses.en: You shall rejoice before him[NOTE:1]—you, your son, your daughter, your male and female slaves, the Levites in your villages,[NOTE:2] the resident foreigners,[NOTE:3] the orphans, and the widows among you—in the place where the Lord chooses to locate his name.
notes: Heb “the Lord your God.” See note on “he” in 16:1.
Heb “gates.”

The ger (גֵּר) “foreign resident” or “naturalized citizen,” (see Exod 12:19 and Deut 29:10-13) could make sacrifices (Lev 17:8; 22:18; Num 15:14) and participate in Israel’s religious festivals: Passover Exod 12:48; Day of Atonement Lev 16:29; Feast of Weeks Deut 16:10-14; Feast of Tabernacles Deut 31:12.
verses.commentary:
16:11 YHWH wants everyone to know His past acts for Israel and His special care for those in need
(cf. Deut. 12:12,18,19; 14:27,29; 16:14; 26:11-13).

verses.zh: 你也要记念你在埃及作过奴仆。你要谨守遵行这些律例。」
verses.en: Furthermore, remember that you were a slave in Egypt, and so be careful to observe these statutes.
verses.commentary:
16:12 "You shall remember" The theological reason for the Feast of Weeks (agricultural harvest) was Israel's
experience of slavery in Egypt.

verses.zh: 「你把禾场的谷、酒榨的酒收藏以后，就要守住棚节七日。
verses.en: You must celebrate the Feast of Shelters[NOTE:1] for seven days, at the time of the grain and grape harvest.[NOTE:2]
notes: The Hebrew phrase חַג הַסֻּכֹּת (khag hassukkot, “Feast of Shelters” or “Feast of Huts”) is traditionally known as the Feast of Tabernacles. The rendering “booths” (cf. NAB, NASB, NRSV) is now preferable to the traditional “tabernacles” (KJV, ASV, NIV) in light of the meaning of the term סֻכָּה (sukkah, “hut; booth”), but “booths” are frequently associated with trade shows and craft fairs in contemporary American English. Clearer is the English term “shelters” (so NCV, TEV, CEV, NLT). This feast was a commemoration of the wanderings of the Israelites after they left Egypt, in which they dwelt in temporary shelters.
Heb “when you gather in your threshing-floor and winepress.”
verses.commentary:
16:13 "Feast of Booths" The Feast of Booths came in the fall and was during the ingathering time
(cf. Exod. 23:16; 34:22; Lev. 23:33-43).

The background to "booths" is said to reflect the Israelites' experience of:

- agricultural life in Egypt, where booths were built in the fields at harvest time to house workers and protect the crop

- living in temporary housing (i.e. tents) during the exodus and wilderness wandering period

- the temporary shelters needed for pilgrims to stay at the central sanctuary (less probable)

SPECIAL TOPIC: FEASTS OF ISRAEL, I. D. 2.

verses.zh: 守节的时候，你和你儿女、仆婢，并住在你城里的利未人，以及寄居的与孤儿寡妇，都要欢乐。
verses.en: You are to rejoice in your festival, you, your son, your daughter, your male and female slaves, the Levites, the resident foreigners, the orphans, and the widows who are in your villages.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “in your gates.”

verses.zh: 在耶和华所选择的地方，你当向耶和华―你的　神守节七日；因为耶和华―你　神在你一切的土产上和你手里所办的事上要赐福与你，你就非常地欢乐。
verses.en: You are to celebrate the festival seven days before the Lord your God in the place he[NOTE:1] chooses, for he[NOTE:2] will bless you in all your productivity and in whatever you do;[NOTE:3] so you will indeed rejoice!
notes: Heb “the Lord.” See note on “he” in 16:1.
Heb “the Lord your God.” See note on “he” in 16:1.
Heb “in all the work of your hands” (so NASB, NIV); NAB, NRSV “in all your undertakings.”
verses.commentary:
16:15 YHWH wants to bless His people so that they may rejoice (BDB 970, KB 1333, Qal PERFECT
with waw) individually, as a family, and as the people of God (cf. Deut. 12:7,12,18; 14:26; 16:11,14; 26:11; 27:7).

verses.zh: 你一切的男丁要在除酵节、七七节、住棚节，一年三次，在耶和华―你　神所选择的地方朝见他，却不可空手朝见。
verses.en: Three times a year all your males must appear before the Lord your God in the place he chooses for the Feast of Unleavened Bread, the Feast of Weeks, and the Feast of Shelters; and they must not appear before him[NOTE:1] empty-handed.
notes: Heb “the Lord.” See note on “he” in 16:1.
verses.commentary:
16:16 "Three times in a year all your males shall appear" Verses 16 and 17 are summary verses which apply
to all three major annual feasts (cf. Exod. 23:14,17). Remember meals were special times of friendship and family fellowship.
These feasts allowed Israel to:

- develop a sense of national community

- teach God's gracious acts to new generations

- help the poor and needy

- rejoice in the goodness of the God of Israel and His fulfillment of covenant promises/blessings

Why only men? Does this reflect the submissive role of women? Surely the ANE was not egalitarian, but
women were honored within Israel (e.g. Proverbs 31).

I think there are two good possibilities:

- the women were needed at home in a ranching and agricultural setting, especially if the men were absent

- the practice of men only would have noticeably marked Israel's worship as different from Canaanite
fertility worship, where women were expected

For a good, brief discussion of these three annual pilgrimage feasts see Roland de Vaux, Ancient Israel,
vol. 2, pp. 484-502.

SPECIAL TOPIC: WOMEN IN THE BIBLE

▣ "Feast" This Hebrew term (BDB 290, KB 290), both the VERB and the NOUN,
refers to one of the three annual worship days at the central sanctuary. It could be translated "pilgrim-feast."

verses.zh: 各人要按自己的力量，照耶和华―你　神所赐的福分，奉献礼物。」
verses.en: Every one of you must give as you are able,[NOTE:1] according to the blessing of the Lord your God that he has given you.
notes: Heb “a man must give according to the gift of his hand.” This has been translated as second person for stylistic reasons, in keeping with the second half of the verse, which is second person rather than third.
verses.commentary:
16:17 "give as he is able" This refers to the universal principle of giving-each is to give as he is able
(cf. Deut. 16:10; 2 Corinthians 8-9).

SPECIAL TOPIC: TITHING

▣ "the blessing" See SPECIAL TOPIC: BLESSING (OT)

verses.zh: 「你要在耶和华―你　神所赐的各城里，按着各支派设立审判官和官长。他们必按公义的审判判断百姓。
verses.en: You must appoint judges and civil servants[NOTE:1] for each tribe in all your villages[NOTE:2] that the Lord your God is giving you, and they must judge the people fairly.[NOTE:3]
notes: The Hebrew term וְשֹׁטְרִים (veshoterim), usually translated “officers” (KJV, NCV) or “officials” (NAB, NIV, NRSV, NLT), derives from the verb שֹׁטֵר (shoter, “to write”). The noun became generic for all types of public officials. Here, however, it may be appositionally epexegetical to “judges,” thus resulting in the phrase, “judges, that is, civil officers,” etc. Whoever the שֹׁטְרִים are, their task here consists of rendering judgments and administering justice.
Heb “gates.”
Heb “with judgment of righteousness”; ASV, NASB “with righteous judgment.”
verses.commentary:
16:18-20 This is a separate section which should go with chapter 18. It deals with guidelines for civil
leadership (tribal judges, Levitical judges, kings, priests, and prophets).

16:18 "You shall appoint for yourself, judges and officers in all your towns" These are the same as the local
elders of the gates (e.g. 21:19; 22:15; Amos 5:10,12,15). Moses was chief judge, but he appointed helpers
(cf. Deut. 1:9-18; Exod.18:13-27).

verses.zh: 不可屈枉正直；不可看人的外貌。也不可受贿赂；因为贿赂能叫智慧人的眼变瞎了，又能颠倒义人的话。
verses.en: You must not pervert justice or show favor. Do not take a bribe, for bribes blind the eyes of the wise and distort[NOTE:1] the words of the righteous.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “twist, overturn”; NRSV “subverts the cause.”
Or “innocent”; NRSV “those who are in the right”; NLT “the godly.”
verses.commentary:
16:19 "You shalt not" This verse lists three guidelines for the judges, Moses' helpers:

- You shalt not distort justice (BDB 639, KB 692, Hiphil IMPERFECT, cf. Exod. 23:6; 27:19;
Deut. 16:19; 24:17; 27:19)

- You shalt not show partiality (BDB 647, KB 699, Hiphil IMPERFECT, the literal Hebrew
is "ye shall not look at a face")

- You shalt not take a bribe (BDB 542, KB 534, Qal IMPERFECT, cf. Deut. 27:25).

▣ "bribe" A bribe does two things:

- "blinds the eyes of the wise" ‒ BDB 734, KB 802, Piel IMPERFECT, cf. Exod. 23:8; it
is metaphorical for the power of money

- "perverts (literally 'twist') the words of the righteous" ‒ BDB 701, KB 758, Piel IMPERFECT,
cf. Exod. 23:8; remember the term "just" or "righteous" is from the term, "measuring reed" or "straight edge."
Most words for sin in the Bible are a word play on this concept.

SPECIAL TOPIC: RIGHTEOUSNESS

verses.zh: 你要追求至公至义，好叫你存活，承受耶和华―你　神所赐你的地。
verses.en: You must pursue justice alone[NOTE:1] so that you may live and inherit the land the Lord your God is giving you.
notes: Heb “justice, justice.” The repetition is emphatic; one might translate as “pure justice” or “unadulterated justice” (cf. NLT “true justice”).
verses.commentary:
16:20 "Justice" A judge ruled according to the standard which was
the revealed will of God ("justice, and only justice"; the MT doubles the NOUN). Leaders
(local and priestly judges) were to model the mercy, yet fairness, of YHWH (cf. Exod. 23:6-8).

▣ "you shall pursue" This VERB (BDB 922, KB 1191, Qal IMPERFECT) is
used literally in Deut. 11:4; 19:6, but here it is imagery of Israel's judicial system. Other uses are found
in Ps. 34:14; Prov. 21:21; Isa. 51:5; and Hosea 6:3.

▣ "that" Israel's possession of the land and the promises/blessings of YHWH were conditional
(cf. Deut. 4:1,25-26,40; 5:16,29,33; 6:18; 8:1; 11:8-9,18-21; 16:20; 32:46-47).

SPECIAL TOPIC: COVENANT

verses.zh: 「你为耶和华―你的　神筑坛，不可在坛旁栽甚么树木作为木偶。
verses.en: You must not plant any kind of tree as a sacred Asherah pole[NOTE:1] near the altar of the Lord your God which you build for yourself.
notes: Sacred Asherah pole. This refers to a tree (or wooden pole) dedicated to the worship of Asherah, wife/sister of El and goddess of fertility. See also Deut 7:5.tn Heb “an Asherah, any tree.”
verses.commentary:
16:21 Deuteronomy 16:21, 22 and 17:1 are one paragraph. The paragraph deals with appropriate ways of
offering sacrifices. For a brief description of Canaanite worship see Alfred J. Hoerth, Archaeology and the Old
Testament, pp. 219-222 and William Foxwell Albright, Archaeology and the Religion of Israel, pp. 67-92.

▣ "You shall not plant. . .an Asherah of any kind of tree" This "grove" or Asherah implies either a grove
of trees or holes in the raised worship platforms of the Canaanites where the carved poles, or live trees representing
the female consort of the male fertility gods, were put. This symbolized fertility worship. See note at Deut. 12:3.

SPECIAL TOPIC: FERTILITY WORSHIP OF THE ANE

verses.zh: 也不可为自己设立柱像；这是耶和华―你　神所恨恶的。
verses.en: You must not erect a sacred pillar,[NOTE:1] a thing the Lord your God detests.
notes: Sacred pillar. This refers to the stelae (stone pillars; the Hebrew term is מַצֵּבֹת, matsevot) associated with Baal worship, perhaps to mark a spot hallowed by an alleged visitation of the gods. See also Deut 7:5.
verses.commentary:
16:22 "You shall not set up for yourself a sacred pillar" See note at Deut. 12:3.

NASB (UPDATED) TEXT: DEUTERONOMY 16:1-8

1"Observe the month of Abib and celebrate the Passover to the Lord
your God, for in the month of Abib the Lord your God brought you out of Egypt by night. 2You shall sacrifice the Passover
to the Lord your God from the flock and the herd, in the place where the Lord chooses to establish His name.
3You shall not eat leavened bread with it; seven days you shall eat with it unleavened bread, the bread of affliction (for you came out of the land of Egypt in haste),
so that you may remember all the days of your life the day when you came out of the land of Egypt. 4For seven days no leaven shall be seen with you in all your
territory, and none of the flesh which you sacrifice on the evening of the first day shall remain overnight until morning. 5You are not allowed to sacrifice the Passover
in any of your towns which the Lord your God is giving you; 6but at the place where the Lord your God
chooses to establish His name, you shall sacrifice the Passover in the evening at sunset, at the time that you came out of Egypt. 7You shall cook and eat it in
the place which the Lord your God chooses. In the morning you are to return to your tents. 8Six days you shall eat unleavened bread,
and on the seventh day there shall be a solemn assembly to the Lord your God; you shall do no work on it."
